correctness.rationale: For each column word, the local bound c_{i-1,r}+c_{i+1,r}+c_{i,1-r}<=1+c_{i,r} is logically equivalent to both definitions of 1-limited domination. Twisted closure c_{i+n}=sigma c_i gives a bijection with weighted paths whose transfer endpoint is J times the initial state. The 16-state transfer is split into symmetric and antisymmetric invariant subspaces. Exact matrix multiplication establishes the seven- and three-dimensional cyclic cores, and their finite determinants equal (1-tz)(1-Q) and 1-tz+t^2 z. The included standard-library program recomputes these determinants via signed permutations rather than relying on claimed output logs. Formal log-derivative traces yield every coefficient for all n>=3, while one-deficit monomial extraction yields degree n or n-1 and multiplicities 4/2n/3n. Direct exhaustive enumeration for n<=10 and independent unreduced 16-state transfer for n<=50 agree. Neither finite experiment is used as the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: An earlier recorded mathematical claim already proves the minimum-size formula and four minimum sets when the rung count is divisible by four; these are explicitly acknowledged as previously covered. The new contribution is a closed rational all-cardinality (1,2)-domination enumerator for every Möbius ladder and explicit 2n/3n multiplicities for the cases not covered by that claim. The three closest primary studies of k-limited and (1,2) domination provide general inequalities and results for other graph families, and do not provide this polynomial. Targeted semantic literature-index queries located no all-cardinality or off-divisible-by-four multiplicity theorem, although index searches cannot establish absolute publication uniqueness.

value.rationale: The new finding determines the complete cardinality profile, not just the previously known optimal domination value, for a canonical infinite family of cubic graphs with a nontrivial antipodal twist. The small factored rational function is explicit and reproducible, and its leading coefficients show a sharp mod-four optimum-multiplicity transition (2n versus 3n off the earlier known 4-divisible case). Such exact-size counts distinguish many feasible dominating configurations and are germane to the recent interest in 1-limited domination on cubic and product graphs. It is not a known-table recomputation or an arbitrary finite slice; all n>=3 and all cardinalities are covered. Limits: no general cubic graph theorem or independence is claimed.
